McLaren.summary: McLaren has tweaked the front of the car – a new, slimmer brake‑duct winglet and a lower cooling scoop – to clean up airflow and keep the engine cool without adding drag. The rear beam wing now runs at a higher angle, using either a single‑ or double‑element version, which gives the car a bit more downforce for the twists and turns of this weekend’s circuit. In short, the changes should help the car stick to the tarmac better and stay stable through the high‑speed sections, giving the team a stronger chance to fight for the podium.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has changed its front suspension to a pull‑rod design and reshaped the brake‑duct area, cleaning up the airflow over the front of the car and giving the brakes and front tyres more bite in the corners. The sidepods are now slimmer with re‑worked cooling exits, tightening the rear‑end aerodynamics while still keeping the engine at optimal temperatures. A fresh rear‑wing profile and a tweaked lower element add extra, more usable down‑force without a big drag penalty, which should translate into better grip and straight‑line speed for the weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull have reshaped the front end – a re‑profiled first‑wing element, new nose fairings and tweaked front‑suspension fairings – to tighten the airflow into the car and give a little extra bite on the corner‑entry. On the floor they’ve moved the fences, added cambered edge surfaces and re‑sculpted the floor and rear‑wing geometry, while a modest side‑pod tweak and smaller cooling louvers help keep the power unit healthy without sacrificing the new downforce gains. In short, the package is all about cleaner aerodynamics and a more stable rear, which should translate into better grip and tyre life for this weekend’s circuit.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: The Mercedes W14 gets a tighter‑pack side‑pod inlet and a deeper under‑cut on the engine cover, letting more clean air hit the car’s front and rear aerodynamics. The floor, beam wing and rear wing have all been reshaped to generate a steadier down‑force balance, while a new low‑profile rear‑track rod at the front helps keep the car stable through corners. Together these tweaks should give the team a bit more grip and consistency on the upcoming circuit, translating into quicker lap times and a stronger fight for podium positions.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: RB’s 2025 C45 shows up with a longer nose that feeds a newly‑shaped front wing and a cleaner‑looking front‑corner air scoop, while the side‑pod inlet has been tucked lower and the engine cover narrowed to tighten the airflow over the car.  Subtle reshapes to the floor, deeper under‑cut, bigger cooling louvres and re‑positioned floor fences add extra rear‑end grip, and the rear‑wing tip is now swept forward with raised beam‑wing tips to give more down‑force without a drag penalty.  A completely revised front‑suspension geometry and refined rear‑suspension fairings round off the package, promising more stable handling and better cornering speed for this weekend’s race.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has lifted and reshaped the side‑pod inlet and given the engine cover a fresh look to tidy up airflow and keep the car cooler, while a full‑floor overhaul – new fences, edges and diffuser – sharpens the downforce the car can generate. The rear corner has been re‑engineered and the wing endplates re‑profiled, plus tweaked rear‑suspension fairings, all aimed at giving the car more grip and a more stable rear on this weekend’s circuit. In short, the upgrades should make the car stick to the tarmac better and keep the tyres in the right window for a stronger race pace.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have fitted a new set of larger, more aggressive cooling louvers – plus an optional grille‑flap on the engine‑cover – that can be added if the track runs hot. They’ve also refined the front‑wing endplates and overall wing loading to keep the airflow smooth around those new cooling pieces. The result should keep the power unit in its sweet spot and give the car a steadier, more predictable feel through the high‑speed corners this weekend.
